answer: A farm emitting 112 variations of one paragraph therefore pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the hollow panel. Because the entropy is measured at the tide gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the glacier audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 3 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. That is 37 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
